author: sonnet
label: c2-seed-sonnet-01
changes: Added a two-sentence summary that says how sessions work today, that the new api_tokens table is the only addition, and why tokens are hashed.
Added a Terms section (token, hash, active token, session, api_tokens table with its columns).

Added a Rules list that restores every fixed requirement the first version dropped: name 1 to 40 characters and unique among active tokens, pat_ plus 32 secure random characters, shown once and never recoverable by support, SHA-256 only with no plaintext in DB, logs or analytics, 90-day non-renewable expiry, limit of 10 active, last-used up to 1 hour stale with no write per request, immediate 401 after revoke with no caching, own tokens only.

Rewrote the diagram so it covers all four flows with the Postgres table and browser or client as labelled participants, and shows failures inline: no session, bad name, limit reached, duplicate name, lost create response, bad token (same generic 401), and a revoke that matches no row.
Merged the vague 'Errors return the usual 4xx codes' into one failures table with a concrete outcome for every case.
Decided and added: the user's row is locked inside the create transaction so concurrent creates cannot exceed 10. Marked as a design decision, not required by the brief.

Decided and added: last-used is updated by one conditional UPDATE only when the value is null or over 1 hour old, which meets the staleness allowance without a cache or per-request write. A failed update does not fail the request.

Decided and added: a lost create response leaves an unseen active token that counts toward the limit. The user revokes it by name and creates another. No resend mechanism is added because the plaintext is unrecoverable.
Decided and added: revoke filters on id and user id and returns 404 for not found, not owned, or already revoked, so other users' tokens are indistinguishable from missing ones.
Added Notes after the diagram for where state lives and the reasoning at create, list, API call and revoke.
Added an Open questions section noting that the exact 400 and 409 status codes are my assumption.
Cut nothing from the first version. It was only the table name, hashing, max 10, 90-day expiry, shown-once and a one-line errors note, and all of that is kept.
